t: Born out of wedlock near Florence and trained in the workshop of Andrea del Verrocchio, Leonardo made his career at the courts of Milan, Florence, Rome and France as a painter, engineer and deviser of pageants.

Fewer than 25 major works are attributed to him, several of them unfinished or ruined by his own experiments in technique, yet the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper are among the most famous and most reproduced paintings in the Western canon.
His notebooks record discoveries in anatomy, hydrodynamics, geology, optics and friction, but he did not publish them, and they had little to no direct influence on later science.
dyk: Most of Leonardo's writings are in mirror-image cursive. He wrote with his left hand, and it was probably easier for him to write from right to left.
ev: Leonardo is born in or close to Vinci in Tuscany, the son of the notary Ser Piero da Vinci and Caterina di Meo Lippi
At the age of 20 he qualifies as a master in the Guild of Saint Luke in Florence, while continuing to work with Verrocchio
He leaves Florence for Milan and the court of Ludovico Sforza, where he works until 1499
He paints The Last Supper for the refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan
He enters the service of Cesare Borgia as military architect and engineer and draws a town plan of Imola
Back in Florence, he begins a portrait of Lisa del Giocondo, the Mona Lisa, on which he works into his later years
He enters the service of King Francis I of France and is given the use of the manor house of Clos Lucé
Leonardo dies at Clos Lucé at the age of 67 and is buried at the Château d'Amboise

f.born: 15 April 1452 in or close to Vinci, a Tuscan hill town about 35 kilometres from Florence; born out of wedlock to Ser Piero da Vinci, a Florentine notary, and Caterina di Meo Lippi, of the lower class
f.died: 2 May 1519 at the manor house of Clos Lucé, near the Château d'Amboise in France, at the age of 67, possibly of a stroke
f.role: Master in the Guild of Saint Luke in Florence from 1472; in the service of Ludovico Sforza in Milan, 1482–1499; military architect and engineer to Cesare Borgia, 1502; in Rome, 1513–1516; in the service of King Francis I of France from 1516
f.known: the Mona Lisa; The Last Supper; the Virgin of the Rocks; the Vitruvian Man drawing; some 13,000 pages of notes and drawings; anatomical drawings made from dissections; designs for flying machines and other devices; the shading technique called sfumato
